_comment: What this deployment sells, as stripe_catalogue.py reads it. Copy this,
put your own products in it, and keep it under version control: the live
catalogue is built from the same file as the test one, which is the only
way the rehearsal proves anything about the real prices.
amount is in minor units - cents - the same unit Stripe uses, so there is
no rounding step to get wrong. 1000 is $10.00.
app is a label for the script's own output, so the printed table says
which app each price id belongs to. Stripe never sees it. name is the
Stripe Product name, which a customer reads on Checkout and on invoices.
tier is what the app asks for at checkout, and what gets stamped on the
workspace's plan. Apps never hold a Stripe id, so repricing is a console
currency defaults to usd, interval to month, interval_count to 1.
